title: AI-Based Intelligent Video Analytics Platform for Border Surveillance using existing CCTV Infrastructure.
department: Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Police II Division
description:
• Background Border security forces deploy CCTV cameras at Border Out Posts(BOPs), check posts, border roads, and other strategic locations for surveillance and monitoring. However, conventional CCTV systems primarily provide video recording and live monitoring capabilities,requiring continuous human observation. Advanced surveillance functionalities such as Facial Recognition Systems (FRS), Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), intrusion detection, and object tracking often require specialized hardware and proprietary solutions,making large-scale deployment costly and difficult, particularly in remote border areas.
• Description The proposed solution aims to develop an AI-driven software platform capable of transforming existing CCTV infrastructure into an intelligent surveillance network without requiring dedicated FRS, ANPR, or smart-camera hardware. The platform shall ingest live video streams from standard IP-based CCTV cameras and perform real-time video analytics using Artificial Intelligence and Computer Vision techniques.
The solution should provide capabilities such as:
• Human detection and tracking
• Vehicle detection and classification
• Face detection
• Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR)
• Virtual fence intrusion detection
• Suspicious activity detection
• Night-time movement detection
• Real-time alert generation and event logging
• Expected Solution The proposed system should leverage Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, and Video Analytics to create a software-defined surveillance platform capable of extracting actionable intelligence from existing CCTV infrastructure.
The solution should:
• Eliminate dependence on expensive dedicated surveillance hardware.
• Enable intelligent monitoring through AI-powered video analytics.
• Provide real-time alerts for security incidents and border intrusions.
• Support facial recognition, vehicle identification, and behavioral analytics through software.
• Improve situational awareness and response time for border security forces.
• Support integration with existing command and control systems.
• The final solution should be cost-effective, scalable, and suitable for deployment across remote border locations and strategic installations.
• Possible Project Name IBVAP – Intelligent Border Video Analytics Platform
summary: Innovation (5/5): draws on ai, artificial intelligence, machine learning applied to a smart automation problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (2/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Smart Automation. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on integration, real-time, infrastructure. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 21/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-Based Intelligent Video Analytics Platform for Border Surveillance using existing CCTV Infrastructure.

overview.in_plain_terms: Take the CCTV cameras already installed at border posts, which today just record video someone has to watch, and add a software layer that automatically detects people, vehicles, faces, and suspicious movement, turning dumb cameras into an intelligent alert system, without buying any new hardware.
overview.why_it_matters: Border forces already have CCTV everywhere, but dedicated smart-camera hardware (with built-in facial recognition, ANPR) is expensive and hard to deploy at scale in remote border areas. A software-only layer that upgrades existing cameras is a genuinely practical, budget-realistic path to better border security.
pain_points: Conventional CCTV requires continuous human observation, which doesn't scale and is prone to fatigue-driven misses.
Advanced capabilities (facial recognition, ANPR, intrusion detection) usually require specialized, proprietary hardware, making large-scale deployment in remote areas costly.
Remote border locations likely have limited bandwidth and power, constraints a cloud-heavy analytics platform would struggle with.
overview.background: Border security forces deploy CCTV at Border Out Posts, check posts, and border roads, but conventional systems only provide recording and live monitoring requiring continuous human observation. Advanced surveillance functionality like FRS, ANPR, and intrusion detection typically needs specialized hardware, making large-scale deployment costly, particularly in remote border areas.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-driven software platform that ingests live video streams from standard IP-based CCTV cameras and performs real-time video analytics, human/vehicle detection and tracking, face detection, ANPR, virtual fence intrusion detection, suspicious activity detection, and night-time movement detection, eliminating dependence on dedicated surveillance hardware, with real-time alerts and integration into existing command and control systems.
expected_solution: Human detection and tracking, vehicle detection and classification, face detection.
Virtual fence intrusion detection and suspicious activity detection.
Real-time alert generation and event logging, integrated with existing command and control systems.
Cost-effective, scalable, deployable on standard CCTV infrastructure.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Breakthrough band, and reasonably so, each individual capability (person detection, ANPR, intrusion detection) is well-established computer vision, but combining seven distinct detection capabilities into one software-only platform running on standard, non-specialized CCTV feeds is a genuinely demanding integration challenge, not a single-model task.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High, correctly scored, this is the widest single-PS feature list in this batch: seven distinct detection capabilities plus real-time alerting plus command-system integration. A team that tries to build all seven at production quality will run out of time; disciplined scoping to 3-4 capabilities is essential.

competitive_landscape.note: CCTV-based AI surveillance/video-analytics is one of the most common SIH PS themes across cycles, judges will have seen many similar pitches (person detection + alerting), differentiation needs to come from actually demonstrating multiple capabilities working together on real or realistic border-like footage, not from any single detection type.

innovation.note: Individual detection capabilities are well-known CV techniques, the innovation is in the software-only, hardware-agnostic integration approach targeting cost-effective deployment.

invention.note: Seven distinct detection capabilities is genuinely broad scope, realistic execution means picking 3-4 to build well rather than attempting all seven shallowly.

technical_feasibility.note: Real-time multi-capability video analytics (person, vehicle, face, ANPR, intrusion, night-vision) simultaneously is a heavy compute ask, be realistic about what runs live versus what's architecturally described.

impact_and_benefits.note: Scored lower on impact reflecting the specialized border-security user base rather than a broad citizen-facing audience, still a high-stakes, well-defined use case within that narrower scope.

architecture.note: Multiple parallel CV pipelines feeding a unified alerting and command-integration layer is genuinely complex systems work for 36 hours.

overall_verdict.reasoning: A crowded but achievable pick if scoped honestly, pick 3-4 of the seven listed capabilities (person detection, virtual fence intrusion, and night-time movement detection are strong, demo-friendly choices) and build those to a genuinely working standard, rather than a shallow pass at all seven. The 'software-only, existing hardware' framing is your strongest differentiator against generic surveillance pitches.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: The 'no new hardware needed' framing is a genuinely compelling, budget-conscious pitch that directly addresses a real deployment barrier for remote border posts.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Attempting all seven listed capabilities will likely mean none work reliably in the live demo, disciplined scoping to a strong subset is essential and should be stated upfront, not hidden.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: which 3-4 of the seven capabilities will be your fully-working demo set, and do you have realistic test footage (public surveillance/border-like video, or recorded footage of your own) to validate against?

idea_0_4: Pick 3-4 capabilities to fully build (recommend: person/vehicle detection, virtual fence intrusion detection, night-time movement detection, these are visually compelling and share underlying detection infrastructure).
Source realistic test footage: public surveillance-style video datasets, or record your own proxy footage simulating a border-post camera angle.
Assign owners: one on the core detection pipeline, one on alerting/event-logging, one on the command-center dashboard UI.
prototype_4_22: Build the core person/vehicle detection and tracking pipeline against your test footage using an off-the-shelf model (YOLO or similar) as your foundation.
Add virtual fence intrusion detection: define a zone in the frame and trigger an alert when a tracked object crosses it.
Build night-time movement detection, testing against low-light footage or simulated low-light conditions.
integration_22_30: Wire detections into a unified real-time alert feed with event logging (timestamp, detection type, location/camera ID).
Build the command-center-style dashboard showing live feed(s) with overlaid detections and an alert queue.
Test across varied footage conditions (day, night, crowded, sparse) to check robustness, and tune thresholds to reduce false-alarm noise.
polish_30_36: Prepare a live demo running detection on real-time or recorded footage, showing the alert feed populate as events occur.
Prepare an honest scope statement: which of the seven capabilities are fully built versus architecturally described as extensions.
Lead the pitch with the cost/deployment story (software-only, existing hardware) as much as the detection accuracy.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Run the detection pipeline live against footage judges haven't seen before, hand them a phone to record a short clip walking past a laptop webcam, and show detection and alerting trigger in real time. Live, unscripted detection is far more convincing than a pre-recorded highlight reel.

strengths: Strong, budget-conscious 'existing hardware' pitch angle directly addresses a real deployment constraint.
Modular capability list allows a focused, deep build on a well-chosen subset.
weaknesses: Very crowded competitive theme, generic person-detection alone won't differentiate against similar pitches.
Seven-capability scope creates strong temptation to overbuild shallowly rather than a focused, working subset.

roles_needed: Backend developer (alerting, event logging, command integration)
team_fit.ideal_ratio: 2 CV-focused to 1 backend/frontend combined, the detection pipeline breadth is the dominant technical challenge.
team_fit.approach: Build a shared detection infrastructure (single video-ingestion and object-tracking base) that multiple capabilities plug into, rather than building each of the 3-4 chosen capabilities as an entirely separate pipeline, this saves real integration time.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Off-the-shelf object detection model integration, basic ANPR via existing OCR libraries, and dashboard UI scaffolding can be built quickly with AI coding assistance.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Tuning intrusion-detection zone logic and false-alarm thresholds against your specific test footage needs iterative human testing, generic defaults will produce a noisy, unconvincing demo.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: Claiming all seven capabilities are 'built' when several are only stubbed-out or untested AI-generated code is the single most likely credibility failure for this PS, given how common and well-understood video-analytics pitches are, judges will likely ask to see specific capabilities live.

data_resource_availability.status: Public surveillance and pedestrian/vehicle-detection datasets are widely available and transfer reasonably well to a border-post-style demo; genuine border-specific footage is not publicly available for obvious security reasons.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If realistic border-post footage can't be sourced, record proxy footage (a hallway, parking lot, or outdoor area simulating a checkpoint) with team members and vehicles, and be upfront that it's a proxy demonstration environment.

judge_qna.question: How does this actually work on 'existing' CCTV infrastructure with no new hardware?
judge_qna.strong_answer: The platform processes standard IP video streams in software, any IP-based camera outputting a compatible stream works, we tested against [your test footage/camera setup] to demonstrate this.
judge_qna.follow_up: What are the minimum bandwidth/resolution requirements for your detection pipeline to work reliably?

judge_qna.question: How do you handle the compute load of running multiple detection models on live video simultaneously?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We [describe your approach, e.g. shared feature extraction across models, frame-sampling strategy, or edge/server split], here's our measured frame rate and latency on our test setup.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your plan for scaling this to dozens of camera feeds simultaneously at a real border post?

judge_qna.question: Why only 3-4 of the seven listed capabilities in your live demo?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We prioritized capabilities with the strongest available test data and clearest demo-able proof within 36 hours, our architecture is modular so additional capabilities plug into the same detection infrastructure.
judge_qna.follow_up: Walk us through what it would take to add ANPR as a fifth working capability.
